entry.title: ANTIOCH-VS: From Sequence to Hits with Modular, Open-Source Ensemble Virtual Screening
entry.summary:
Structure-based virtual screening needs a receptor conformation that fits the ligand class, but for most targets no ligand-bound crystal is available -- and a single predicted model or an apo structure often misses the binding-competent state. We present ANTIOCH-VS, an open-source framework that runs an entire in silico screening campaign, from a protein sequence to a ranked shortlist of candidate binders, as one plug-and-play workflow. It first builds a conformational ensemble by reduced-MSA subsampling with ColabFold, then uses AlphaFold2-RAVE (AF2RAVE) -- short molecular-dynamics simulations with State Predictive Information Bottleneck analysis -- to pick out docking-ready, Boltzmann-weighted metastable states.

Source: arXiv Quantitative Biology & Materials (q-bio, mtrl-sci) · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #consensus

entry.title: Bridging Graph and Pairwise Learning for Gene Regulatory Network Inference from scRNA-seq Data
entry.summary:
Motivation: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) capture the underlying interactions through which transcription factors (TFs) regulate genes. Based on gene expression data, existing GRN inference approaches generally fall into two categories: graph-based methods, which model the GRN as a whole graph, and pairwise-based methods, which decompose the GRN into individual TF-target gene pairs for modeling. However, each approach exhibits limitations that are precisely the strengths of its counterpart.

Source: arXiv Quantitative Biology & Materials (q-bio, mtrl-sci) · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #ml-theory #combinatorics

entry.title: Detection of local recombination and mutation hotspots in bacterial genomes using neural posterior estimation
entry.summary:
Motivation: Recombination and mutation rates in bacteria vary along the genome, and regions of elevated rate (hotspots) often reflect selection on specific genes. Detecting them is difficult because the two processes leave overlapping signals in sequence data, clonal relationships act as a confounder, and inference must scale to whole genomes. Existing methods assume a constant mutation rate and/or rely on a small set of summary statistics.

Source: arXiv Quantitative Biology & Materials (q-bio, mtrl-sci) · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #neuroscience

entry.title: Detection of Maximal Exact Matches in Terabases of Genome Assemblies in Compressed Space and Sublinear Time
entry.summary:
Detection of long exact matches between a pair of genomes has historically been a fundamental operation in genomics. Similarly, detection of long exact matches between all pairs of haplotypes in a large panel of genotyping array data or whole-genome sequencing variant calls is a fundamental operation in population genetics. Thanks to various recent pangenome efforts, for the first time, large panels of high-quality genome assemblies are being constructed.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: SIFT: Syncmer-Informed Selection of Haplotypes for T2T Imputation. Genome patching improves the completeness of fragmented assemblies by filling unresolved gaps with sequences from reference genomes.
entry.summary:
Genome patching improves the completeness of fragmented assemblies by filling unresolved gaps with sequences from reference genomes. Pangenome panels provide diverse candidate haplotypes for this task, but identifying suitable references efficiently becomes increasingly challenging as these panels grow. We present SIFT, a compressed indexing method for selecting reference haplotypes for genome patching with ImpuT2T.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: Reticulation-Aware Dissimilarities for Phylogenetic Networks. Dissimilarity measures play a critical role in phylogenetics.
entry.summary:
Dissimilarity measures play a critical role in phylogenetics. They help quantify the accuracy of inferences when the ground truth is known, allow comparisons of inferences obtained using different methods, and provide a tool for summarizing sets of phylogenies. A wide array of dissimilarity measures has been introduced for phylogenetic trees over the past half-century, and they vary in their mathematical properties, empirical behavior, and computational complexity.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: ProClust provides reliable statistical significance of clusters for single-cell transcriptomic data
entry.summary:
Clustering of single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data is widely used to identify cell populations. However, overclustering can partition a single cell population into multiple clusters, potentially leading to spurious identification of cell subpopulations. Assessing the statistical significance of clusters is therefore needed to support their biological interpretation.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: Batch, Prefetch, Skip, Orient, Squeeze: Faster, Smaller k-mer dictionaries via the Spectral Burrows-Wheeler transform
entry.summary:
Looking up k-mers in an index is a core operation in genomics, underlying read mapping, metagenomic classification, and many other tasks. Queries are often streaming: the k-mers come from a longer sequence such as a sequencing read, and consecutive k-mers overlap. The fastest index for such queries is currently the hashing-based SSHash; indexes based on the spectral Burrows-Wheeler transform (SBWT) are competitive in space but slower.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #infosec

entry.title: Ab initio simulation of excited-state potential energy surfaces with transferable deep quantum Monte Carlo
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01065-y Transferable deep-learning quantum Monte Carlo for molecular excited states is introduced. Sharing parameters, an ansatz represents the wavefunction across molecular geometries and states, reducing the cost of modeling potential energy surfaces.

Source: Nature Computational Science · Tags: #bioinformatics #materials-science
